lines.text: A hand-cranked, gear-driven handheld fan: no motor, no battery, every part 3D printed.
Stage one: the CAD model, the team's own assembly.
Exploded along its shafts: two shell halves, a crank, three gears, two shafts, three axle pins, a propeller.
The crank's fifty-four-tooth gear drives a twelve-tooth pinion on a compound gear, whose large gear drives the propeller's pinion.
Two speed-up stages: in theory, about twenty propeller turns per crank turn.
CAD is where fit, alignment, centre distance and clearance are checked, before printing.
Stage two: STL export. Each part gets its own file, as each is printed separately.
lines.say: Stage two: S T L export. Each part gets its own file, as each is printed separately.

lines.text: The exact CAD surfaces become a mesh of flat triangles.
The mesh is checked: closed, normals outward, scale in millimetres; then oriented for printing.
Stage three: slicing. Parts lie flat on the plate: shells open side up, gears flat, so each tooth forms within every layer.
The slicer cuts each part into thin layers and plans every toolpath: walls, then infill.
The report suggests finer layers and extra walls for gears; supports go only where an overhang needs them.
Stage four: FDM printing. Filament is melted in a heated nozzle and laid along the planned path.
lines.say: Stage four: F D M printing. Filament is melted in a heated nozzle and laid along the planned path.

lines.text: The first layer bonds to the bed; the nozzle then rises one layer, and each layer fuses to the last.
Nothing is cut away: the gear is built up, teeth first, then its pinion.
Shell walls grow the same way, leaving fine layer lines.
When the print ends, the bed cools before parts are removed.
Stage five: finishing. A printed part is not yet a mechanism.
Brims and strings are trimmed; gear flanks and shafts are sanded to remove layer ridges.
Pin holes are reamed so shafts turn freely, and the gears are lubricated.
Balanced on its shaft, the propeller should stop at random angles.
Stage six: assembly and test. The crank gear, compound gear and propeller pinion go into the shell, meshing.
The second shell closes the train; the crank handle, propeller and cap go on last.
By design, the crank drives both gear stages, so the propeller spins far faster than the hand.
The test plan: fit, free rotation, speed ratio, airflow, endurance and balance. Results are still to be measured.
From CAD model to finished product: one digital design, six stages, no tooling.
